cards.front: Recall a key point about Augustus & the Principate
cards.back: Octavian (later Augustus) was Caesar's adopted heir who defeated Mark Antony at Actium (31 BC) to become Rome's sole ruler

cards.front: Recall a key point about Augustus & the Principate
cards.back: The Second Triumvirate (43 BC): Octavian, Antony and Lepidus divided the Roman world; it ended in civil war between Octavian and Antony

cards.front: Recall a key point about Augustus & the Principate
cards.back: Augustus established the Principate: he held supreme power but maintained Republican forms and titles (Princeps = First Citizen)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Augustus & the Principate
cards.back: The constitutional settlement (27 BC): Augustus 'restored the Republic' but kept consulship, tribunician power and control of key provinces

cards.front: Recall a key point about Augustus & the Principate
cards.back: The Pax Romana (Roman Peace) brought stability, prosperity and cultural flourishing across the empire

cards.front: Recall a key point about Augustus & the Principate
cards.back: Augustus reformed the army, morality, religion and building programme; he boasted he 'found Rome brick and left it marble'

cards.front: What should you know about gcse ancient history exam tips — augustus & the principate?
cards.back: 1. For Augustus & the Principate, include specific factual detail: dates, names, events and statistics where relevant 2. For source questions, analyse provenance (who, when, why, audience) before using the content 3. In evaluation questions, discuss multiple factors and weigh their relative significance 4. Always link back to the question focus — don't just narrate what happened with Augustus & the Principate 5. Use phrases like 'the most significant factor was... because...' to show analytical judgement
Explain how Augustus established the Principate and describe how he maintained the illusion of the Republic while holding supreme power. [6 marks]
